content.comment_body: I have a [product_name] controller ([article_no]) expanded with [article_no]. I can see additional inputs and outputs in the diagnostic menu, but activating any output via the program or input signal has no effect. It seems the controller is not using any connected I/Os from the module. In the programming interface, I haven't found settings to add extension modules to the controller, only network or master/slave configurations. Am I missing something? I believe its firmware is [version_no]. Regards.

Is the LED on the expansion module green? Red indicates a problem. Did you slide the switch on the expansion unit (the small gray block) to the left? Don't forget to remove the small plastic lid from the basic [product_name]. You can also read about this in the documents included in the box.
I can read more I/Os in the [product_name] controller when the extension module is powered, so the light is clearly green and the communication plug is correctly connected.

If you add expansion modules to the [product_name], you don't need to configure them in the program—this happens automatically. However, your program should account for these expansion units. For example, if no expansion modules are installed, you can try to control digital output 5 in your program and nothing will occur. But you can still use output 5 as a marker.

That's exactly what I did. I manually activated inputs on the extension card and got no response, and even when assigning an "always high" signal to the fifth output, none of the extension outputs worked.

Are you sure your [product_name] is [article_no] version? Is your extension unit the [article_no] version? Are both the basic unit and expansion unit powered with approximately 230V AC? Is the green LED on the expansion unit on? Be aware that the [product_name] and the expansion unit use potential-free contacts. If all of these are correct, then your extension unit might be faulty.

I've identified the cause of the issue. The screws on the extension unit are isolated when open. To measure I/Os, you need to connect cables or fully screw in the I/O terminals so you can check outputs with a tester.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced a situation where the expansion module's I/Os appeared in diagnostics but were unresponsive to program commands or manual activation. Further conversation clarified that proper wiring—specifically, making sure terminal screws were tightened—was required for reliable I/O operation, not just attaching and powering the module.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expected automatic recognition and operation of I/Os on the expansion module without further steps beyond installation and powering up, assuming that all acknowledged connections would work immediately for both testing and programming.
